'''Peter Edward Kaus''' (October 9, 1924 – November 6, 2016) was an Austrian-born American physicist.

== Early life and career ==
Kaus was born in [[Vienna]], the son of Otto Sr. and [[Gina Kaus]], a novelist and screenwriter. He attended the [[Schottengymnasium]] until 1938. He was the brother of [[Otto Kaus]], an associate justice of the [[Supreme Court of California]]. He and his family emigrated to [[France]], settling in [[Paris]], and then emigrated to the United States, settling in [[Hollywood, California]]. He attended [[Hollywood High School]], graduating in 1940. After graduating, he attended the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), but his education was interrupted when he enlisted in the armed forces during [[World War II]]. After his discharge, he returned to UCLA, and earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[physics]] in 1954, which after earning his degree, he moved to [[Princeton, New Jersey]], and then moved to [[Riverside, California]] in 1963.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/in-memoriam/files/peter-kaus.html|title=Peter Edward Kaus|work=[[University of California|Academic Senate]]|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>

Kaus served as a professor in the department of physics at the [[University of California, Riverside]] from 1967 to 1994.<ref name="a" /> During his years as a professor, in 1969, he was named a [[Lists of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=peter%20kaus&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref> and in 1986, he was named an honorary trustee of the [[Aspen Center for Physics]].<ref name="a" />

== Personal life and death ==
Kaus was married to Eva Lewy, and they had three daughters. Their marriage lasted until Kaus's death in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aspentimes.com/obituaries/peter-kaus/|title=Peter Kaus|work=[[The Aspen Times]]|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>

Kaus died at his home on November 6, 2016, at the age of 92.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dcourier.com/obituaries/obituary-peter-kaus/article_b9dfb27d-0c2c-52b2-9dd2-38543cf9d25a.html|title=Obituary: Peter Kaus|work=The Daily Courier|date=November 10, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>
